newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says nearly 56 mln to vote in council poll.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says nearly 56 mln to vote in council poll.

text.p: Nigeria's electoral commission said on Thursday almost 56 million people had been registered to vote in Saturday's local council polls -- a test of the military government's commitment to restoring democracy.

Commission chairman Sumner Dagogo-Jack told a news conference in the capital Abuja that the figure was five million above the projected 1996 figure of eligible voters worked out by the population commision.
"From our analysis schedule, a total of 55,714,773 million voters have been registered throughout the country," he said.
Saturday's election, rescheduled from the last quarter of last year, would be the first to test the strength of the country's five registered political parties.
Electioneering reached fever pitch on Thursday, the last day for of campaigning, with television and radio jingles, rallies and posters promising everything for a vote.
Jide Damazio, a 43-year-old microbiologist vying for the chairman of Lagos Island, promised "Food for all" and "Education without tears" if elected.
A 38-strong delegation from the United States comprising political activists, religious leaders and journalists has arrived in Nigeria to monitor the polls.

"We are here to voluntarily observe the elections," said the group's spokeswoman Joan Wallace when they met the influential minister of the federal capital Abuja, Lieutenant-General Jeremiah Useni, on Wednesday.
Nigeria has been shunned by Western countries for lack of democracy and human rights violations.
Its last attempt at democracy ended in chaos when the previous military ruler annulled a presidential vote in 1993.
Military ruler General Sani Abacha seized power in the aftermath of the annulment. He is implementing a transition plan he has drawn up to hand over to an elected president on October 1, 1998.
